statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail risk is low at 9% after NQ round-tripped its Globex advance and returned to within 18.50 points of the overnight low.
recommendation: Tail sits well below the block threshold, so the mapped state stays EA_ON. The 13:00-15:00 UTC window covering the Williams speech, the U.S. cash open and the Bowman speech is the session's main checkpoint, where the published forecast reaches WATCH. headline: NQ gives back its overnight advance and returns toward the Globex low, leaving the retracement intact
body: Nasdaq-100 futures trade at 31,344.00, up 26.25 points (+0.08%), after failing to hold the 31,410.75 Globex high reached in the previous hour and easing roughly 67 points from it. Price now sits just 18.50 points above the overnight low at 31,325.50, so the entire advance of the Asian session has been retraced inside an 85.25-point range worth about 0.27% of index value. That round trip is the decisive observation: the overnight move was given back rather than extended, which is working mean reversion and not the persistent one-way path the Tail score is designed to detect. The fade is corroborated across risk assets. E-mini S&P 500 futures at 7,832.00 (+0.07%) are likewise near the low of a narrow 7,829.00-7,838.50 range, and the Nikkei 225 has slipped to 70,140.70 (+0.28%) from a session high of 70,416.78, so Asian equities are fading their highs in the same direction rather than driving futures onward. The cash index closed on 5 October at a record 31,076.44, up 268.51 points (+0.87%), with a record intraday high of 31,117.36, led by Nvidia's record close near $237 and broad artificial-intelligence strength. The persistent tension in this tape is the bond market: the 10-year yield stands at 5.31%, up three basis points and close to its highest level since 2002, with the 2-year at 4.83% on the latest H.15 release, while the ISM services index for September slowed to 54.9 from 55.4 and its prices component rose to 74.0 from 72.6. Equities advancing against yields at multi-decade highs is a cross-asset conflict rather than an alignment, and under the operating contract a conflict of that kind raises Stress and tempers conviction rather than mechanically raising Tail. Volatility remains contained with VIX at 15.52, and WTI crude at $89.70 is firm but stable. Against that backdrop Tail falls to 9%, Stress eases to 45% on compressing realised volatility, and Confidence holds at 86% on fresh verified futures, index, volatility, yield and energy evidence. The shared Finviz context file was last collected on 29 September and is reported partial, so it fails the 90-minute freshness test and was excluded from this assessment; the independent research above carries it instead.

lookbackSummary: The prior 24 hours of published Claude assessments stayed in the low Tail band apart from the 19:00 UTC hour, which reached WATCH at 20% during the U.S. afternoon advance to a record close. Tail ran from 13% in the Asian session on 5 October down to 6% by 08:00 UTC, climbed through the European and U.S. sessions to that 20% peak at 19:00 UTC, then decayed to 9% by 00:00 UTC before a brief 12% reading at 01:00 UTC when NQ printed a new Globex high. Stress fell steadily from 60% to 46% as realised volatility compressed even while yields stayed near multi-decade highs, and Confidence held between 85% and 89% throughout. The 06:00 UTC hour has no published assessment and is recorded as unavailable rather than reconstructed.
outlookSummary: The published path keeps Tail in the low band for 22 of the 24 forecast hours and reaches WATCH only at 13:00 and 14:00 UTC, which span the Williams speech, the U.S. cash open and the Bowman speech. Tail holds near 9-10% through the thin late-Asian hours, steps up from the European cash open at 08:00 UTC, peaks at 21% in the first full U.S. cash hour, then decays through the afternoon with a secondary 16% reading in the power hour into the 20:00 UTC cash close before easing to 10% by the Asian session on 7 October. Stress tracks the same shape between 44% and 56%. Confidence declines from 86% to 77% across the window as distance from the verified overnight price evidence grows. Every hour beyond the current clock hour is conditional: no European or U.S. price path has been observed at assessment time, and the scheduled items listed in the event calendar are checkpoints rather than assertions about outcomes.
